name: Amazon Connect Contact Center Lens - Global Resiliency
description: Amazon Connect Well-Architected Contact Center Lens for Global Resiliency.

questions.title: What configuration options to enable Amazon Connect Global Resiliency do you have in place today?
questions.description: Prior to deploying Amazon Connect Global Resiliency, ensure you have completed the necessary technical and operational pre-requisites.

choices.title: Ported all phone numbers you want to enable for use with Amazon Connect Global Resiliency

helpfulResource.displayText: In order to use Traffic Distribution Groups within Global Resiliency, the phone numbers must be claimed in your Amazon Connect instance. Numbers acquired within Amazon Connect or ported into Amazon Connect are eligible.

improvementPlan.displayText: Ensure that the phone numbers you want to use for Global Resiliency are associated with your Amazon Connect instance..

choices.title: Created a Test SAML 2.0-enabled Amazon Connect instance where ACGR is available (us-east-1/us-west-2 or eu-west-2/eu-central-1)

helpfulResource.displayText: Amazon Connect supports identity federation by configuring Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) 2.0 with AWS IAM to enable web-based single sign-on (SSO) from your organization to your Amazon Connect instance. This allows your users to sign in to a portal in your organization hosted by a SAML 2.0 compatible identity provider (IdP) and log in to an Amazon Connect instance with a single sign-on experience without having to provide separate credentials for Amazon Connect.

improvementPlan.displayText: Create and onboard your test environment to Global Resiliency prior to production accounts.

choices.title: Created a Prod SAML 2.0-enabled Amazon Connect instance where ACGR is available (us-east-1/us-west-2 or eu-west-2/eu-central-1)

helpfulResource.displayText: Amazon Connect supports identity federation by configuring Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) 2.0 with AWS IAM to enable web-based single sign-on (SSO) from your organization to your Amazon Connect instance. This allows your users to sign in to a portal in your organization hosted by a SAML 2.0 compatible identity provider (IdP) and log in to an Amazon Connect instance with a single sign-on experience without having to provide separate credentials for Amazon Connect.

improvementPlan.displayText: Ensure that you have a SAML enabled instance created before proceeding with onboarding.

choices.title: Tested in a lower environment prior to production.

helpfulResource.displayText: It is recommended to create and maintain a dev or test environment for testing prior to making production changes.

improvementPlan.displayText: Test your Amazon Connect Global Resiliency configuration in a lower environment prior to a production go-live

choices.title: For agent failover, Custom or Embedded CCP developed using Streams API, or Agent Workspace.

helpfulResource.displayText: Amazon Connect Agent Workspace and Custom or Embedded CCP support ACGR Global Sign-in. The Amazon Connect Streams API (Streams) gives you the power to integrate your existing web applications with Amazon Connect. Streams lets you embed the Contact Control Panel (CCP) and Customer Profiles app UI into your page. It also enables you to handle agent and contact state events directly through an object-oriented event driven interface. You can use the built-in interface or build your own from scratch: Streams gives you the choice.

improvementPlan.displayText: Utilize Agent Workspace or the Streams API to facilitate an automated agent failover

helpfulResource.displayText: Choose this option if none of these configuration options are in place today.

questions.title: Does your organization have well understood and defined RTO and RPO targets?
questions.description: RTO and RPO are your objectives for restoration of your workload. Set these based on business needs. Implement a strategy to meet these objectives, considering locations and function of workload resources and data. The probability of disruption and cost of recovery are also key factors that help to inform the business value of providing disaster recovery for a workload.

helpfulResource.displayText: A mix of RPO and RTO can range from standby to active-active implementations

improvementPlan.displayText: Ensure your RPO and RTO objectives align with your business, regulatory, and other requirements

helpfulResource.displayText: Choose this option if your organization doesn't have RTO and RPO targets.

questions.title: What multi region strategy are you considering?
questions.description: Disaster recovery strategies available to you within AWS can be broadly categorized into four approaches, ranging from the low cost and low complexity of making backups to more complex strategies using multiple active Regions. Note: With Global Routing, Amazon Connect supports cross-region contact routing. The routing engine evaluates agents across both regions and can route a contact originating in one region to an available agent in the other, so neither region starves while the other has surplus capacity.

helpfulResource.displayText: Backup and restore is a suitable approach for mitigating against data loss or corruption. This approach can also be used to mitigate against a regional disaster by replicating data to other AWS Regions. In addition to data, you must redeploy the infrastructure, configuration, and application code in the recovery Region.

improvementPlan.displayText: Consider if the RTO and RPO provided by a Backup & Restore strategy is worth the deployment or downtime cost.

helpfulResource.displayText: With the pilot light approach, you replicate your data from one Region to another and provision a copy of your core workload infrastructure. Resources required to support data replication and backup, such as databases and object storage, are always on. Other elements, such as application servers, are loaded with application code and configurations, but are 'switched off' and are only used during testing or when disaster recovery failover is invoked.

improvementPlan.displayText: Many services used with Amazon Connect are consumption based. Consider if Pilot Light is the most effective approach, or if an approach with a lower RTO and RPO is more appropriate. The pilot light approach requires you to 'turn on' servers, possibly deploy additional (non-core) infrastructure, and scale up, whereas hot standby only requires you to shift traffic (everything is already deployed and running).

helpfulResource.displayText: The hot standby approach involves ensuring that there is an inactive, but fully functional, copy of your production environment in another Region. This approach extends the pilot light concept and decreases the time to recovery because your workload is always-on in another Region. When traffic is shifted to the replica region, it is capable of handling the production workload..

improvementPlan.displayText: This approach allows you to more easily perform testing or implement continuous testing to increase confidence in your ability to recover from a disaster.

helpfulResource.displayText: You can run your workload simultaneously in multiple Regions as part of a multi-site active/active. Multi-site active/active serves traffic from all regions to which it is deployed. With a multi-site active/active approach, users are able to access your workload in any of the Regions in which it is deployed.

improvementPlan.displayText: This approach is the most complex and costly approach to disaster recovery, but it can reduce your recovery time to near zero for most disasters with the correct technology choices and implementation. With multi-site active/active, because the workload is running in more than one Region, there is no such thing as failover in this scenario. Disaster recovery testing in this case would focus on how the workload reacts to loss of a Region: Is traffic routed away from the failed Region? Can the other Region(s) handle all the traffic?

helpfulResource.displayText: Choose this option if your Amazon Connect Global Resiliency doesn't match any of the options listed.

questions.title: How have you configured your Traffic Distribution Groups (TDG)?
questions.description: Traffic distribution groups allow you to configure how your telephony traffic and agents are routed between Amazon Connect instances. You can configure the distribution for groups of phone numbers and agents, in 10 percent intervals, between paired instances.

choices.title: Each line of business is in their own TDG.

helpfulResource.displayText: You can choose to create separate TDGs for your different lines of business if they have separate phone numbers and agents. This allows you shift traffic and agents for critical business or functions without moving all traffic.

improvementPlan.displayText: Identify how you would like to distribute your traffic and agents across your business.

choices.title: All numbers and agents are in a single TDG.

helpfulResource.displayText: You can choose to move all numbers and agents from one region to another at the same time. This allows for the minimal configuration, but does not allow for testing of non-prod numbers.

improvementPlan.displayText: Identify how you would like to distribute your traffic and agents across your business.

choices.title: All production numbers and agents are in one TDG and all test numbers and agents are in another TDG.

helpfulResource.displayText: You can choose to move all numbers and agents from one region to another at the same time in production and test buckets.

improvementPlan.displayText: Identify how you would like to distribute your traffic and agents across your business.

helpfulResource.displayText: If you have a different strategy for your TDGs, include it in the notes.

improvementPlan.displayText: Identify how you would like to distribute your traffic across your business.

helpfulResource.displayText: Choose this option if your TDGs haven't been configured.

questions.title: What does your failover runbook address?
questions.description: If your recovery point objective is one hour, then you need to detect the incident, notify appropriate personnel, engage your escalation processes, evaluate information (if you have any) on expected time to recovery (without executing the DR plan), declare a disaster and recover within an hour. Ensure that you have documented and tested the people and technology required to successfully execute a failover.

helpfulResource.displayText: Monitoring Amazon Connect and other AWS services used in your Contact Center is important to discover anomalies or unusual behavior in system state and performance, this will provide valuable data that can be analyzed as part of the Business Continuity Process (BCP) and Standard Operation Procedures (SOP) defined in your ACGR Runbook before the decision is made to failover to the replica region.

improvementPlan.displayText: Monitoring Amazon Connect and other AWS services used in your Contact Center will provide data points for the operations team to be alerted that the workload is not delivering the business outcomes that they should be delivering. In this way, you can quickly declare a disaster and recover from an incident.

choices.title: The scenarios that would require a traffic distribution change to be initiated

helpfulResource.displayText: AWS publishes our most up-to-the-minute information on service availability on the Service Health Dashboard. Check at any time to get current status information, or subscribe to an RSS feed to be notified of interruptions to each individual service. If you are experiencing a real-time, operational issue with one of our services that is not shown on the Service Health Dashboard, you can create a Support Request.

improvementPlan.displayText: It is important to know as soon as possible that your workloads are not delivering the business outcomes that they should be delivering. In this way, you can quickly declare a disaster and recover from an incident.

choices.title: The mechanism to initiate a telephony failover.

helpfulResource.displayText: After you have claimed phone numbers to your traffic distribution group, use the UpdateTrafficDistribution API to distribute telephony traffic across linked instances in a given traffic distribution group in 10 percent increments.

improvementPlan.displayText: Ensure you have a documented process for invoking the UpdateTrafficDistribution API. This can be done via the CLI, API, or a custom UI. Ensure that the appropriate stakeholders have access to perform this action and that the process is documented..

helpfulResource.displayText: You should assign agents to your traffic distribution group, for agents using the Global Sign-in URL and Agent Workspace or Custom CCP with Streams API, use the UpdateTrafficDistribution API to distribute agent traffic across linked instances in a given traffic distribution group in 10 percent increments. For Agents using the regional endpoint the failover is performed by manually logging out of the impacted region and logging into the replica region.

improvementPlan.displayText: Ensure the agent failover process is documented and your agents and supervisors are trained on how to properly shift to the replica region.

choices.title: Under what conditions would traffic be returned back to the initial source AWS region

helpfulResource.displayText: The AWS Health Dashboard provides information about AWS Health events that can affect your account. You can also implement health checks to validate when the source environment is recovered and you can return traffic.

improvementPlan.displayText: Design health checks that are representative of user experience and based on Key Performance Indicators. Deep health checks exercise key functionality of your workload and go beyond shallow heartbeat checks. Use deep health checks based on multiple signals.

choices.title: Why and how you move a particular traffic distribution group before another

helpfulResource.displayText: Business impact may be time dependent. You may want to consider factoring this in to your disaster recovery planning. For example, disruption to your payroll system is likely to have a very high impact to the business just before everyone gets paid, but it may have a low impact just after everyone has already been paid.

improvementPlan.displayText: If you have priority business units, ensure that is included in your alerting and failover plans. Document the conditions that would require one business unit to shift traffic, and what would require additional business units to shift traffic.

choices.title: Frequent testing to ensure operational readiness.

helpfulResource.displayText: Our experience has shown that the only error recovery that works is the path you test frequently. This is the reason why having a small number of recovery paths is best. You can establish recovery patterns and regularly test them. If you have a complex or critical recovery path, you still need to regularly execute that failure in production to validate that the recovery path works.

improvementPlan.displayText: Test disaster recovery implementation to validate the implementation and regularly test failover to your workloads DR Region to ensure that RTO and RPO are met.

helpfulResource.displayText: Choose this option if your disaster recovery runbook does not follow these best practices.

questions.title: Under what conditions would you recover back to the initial source AWS region?
questions.description: In a DR scenario, you need a simple and effective approach to mitigate failures and then return to normal operations. To be fast and reliable, this process must be straightforward, require minimal steps, and be practiced regularly.

choices.title: Shifting of numbers and agents back to prior region and performing validation.

helpfulResource.displayText: Traffic Distribution Groups allow you to shift traffic and agents in 10 percent increments. When validating health of the source region, traffic can be slowly moved back so test plans can be executed.

improvementPlan.displayText: Determine at what rate traffic and agents would be returned to the source region. Determine what the testing process is for validating health of the environment.

helpfulResource.displayText: AWS publishes our most up-to-the-minute information on service availability on the Service Health Dashboard. Check at any time to get current status information, or subscribe to an RSS feed to be notified of interruptions to each individual service. If you are experiencing a real-time, operational issue with one of our services that is not shown on the Service Health Dashboard, you can create a Support Request. The AWS Health Dashboard provides information about AWS Health events that can affect your account.

improvementPlan.displayText: Monitoring the health dashboards will provide you with updates and signals as service restoration occurs. Use this data to influence when to return traffic to the source region.

helpfulResource.displayText: Confirmation from AWS Support

improvementPlan.displayText: Confirmation from AWS Support

questions.title: What is your telephony failover mechanism?
questions.description: Traffic failover is performed with the UpdateTrafficDistribution API. This can be done via the CLI, API, or a custom UI.

choices.title: Manually initiate the failover API on the necessary traffic distribution groups

helpfulResource.displayText: For more information about creating traffic distribution groups, see Set up traffic distribution groups in the Amazon Connect Administrator Guide.

improvementPlan.displayText: Ensure that the process for invoking the UpdateTrafficDistribution API aligns to your RTO and RPO targets.

choices.title: Automated process that monitors production numbers.

helpfulResource.displayText: It is important to know as soon as possible that your workloads are not delivering the business outcomes that they should be delivering. In this way, you can quickly declare a disaster and recover from an incident. For aggressive recovery objectives, this response time coupled with appropriate information is critical in meeting recovery objectives.

improvementPlan.displayText: For the most stringent RTO requirements, you can implement automated failover based on health checks. Design health checks that are representative of user experience and based on Key Performance Indicators.

helpfulResource.displayText: Choose this option if your failover mechanism does not follow these best practices.

questions.title: What is your agent failover mechanism?
questions.description: Unless your DR strategy consists of operating IVR-only workloads, once traffic is shifted to a replica region agents need to be logged into the replica instance.

choices.title: For agents using Global Sign-in URL, manually initiate the failover API on the necessary traffic distribution groups.

helpfulResource.displayText: For agents using the Global Sign-in URL and Agent Workspace or Custom CCP with Streams API, Amazon Connect Global Resiliency enables you to provide a global experience for agents with global sign-in, agent distribution API, and Agent Workspace enhancements. This will enable your agents to sign in once at the beginning of their day and process contacts from their current active Region without needing to know which Region is active at any time.

improvementPlan.displayText: Appropriate process documentation, communication, and testing helps ensure agents are aware of what to do in case of failover.

choices.title: For Agents using the regional endpoint URL, instruct agents to log out of source instance and launch replica instance.

helpfulResource.displayText: You may choose to only expose the replica instance in your SSO portal when necessary, or automatically redirect logins to the active instance via a vanity URL or other mechanism.

improvementPlan.displayText: Appropriate process documentation, communication, and testing helps ensure agents can successfully failover to the replica region.

choices.title: Handle the active instance via a custom CCP

helpfulResource.displayText: The Amazon Connect Streams API (Streams) gives you the power to integrate your existing web applications with Amazon Connect. Streams lets you embed the Contact Control Panel (CCP) UI into your page. It also enables you to handle agent and contact state events directly through an object-oriented event driven interface.

improvementPlan.displayText: Ensure the agent failover process is documented and your agents and supervisors are trained on how to properly shift to the replica region.

choices.title: Agents run active-active across both regions via TDG. Agent failover is still required during a regional impairment.

helpfulResource.displayText: Global Routing distributes agents across both ACGR regions simultaneously (e.g., 50-50 via TDG), and the routing engine directs contacts to the optimal agent regardless of region. Under normal active-active operation, agent failover is not essential because agents are already active in both regions. However, agent failover is still required during a regional impairment: when agents can no longer sign in to or operate in the impaired region, you must shift that agent capacity to the healthy region using the Traffic Distribution (TDG) APIs.

improvementPlan.displayText: Document in your runbook that, in normal active-active operation, no agent failover action is needed. For a regional impairment, define the procedure to fail agents over from the impaired region to the healthy region (e.g., shifting sign-in distribution from 50-50 to 0-100) using UpdateTrafficDistribution, so agents who cannot sign in to the impaired region can operate from the healthy region.

helpfulResource.displayText: Choose this option if your failover mechanism does not follow these best practices.

questions.title: Are you checking whether agents have completed their active interactions before failing them over?
questions.description: Shifting agent logins can be disruptive if they are actively participating in a non-voice interaction.

helpfulResource.displayText: The Amazon Connect agent event stream can provide details on agent state

improvementPlan.displayText: If using automated methods, check whether the agent has completed their active contact prior to moving them to the replica region.

helpfulResource.displayText: Agents fail over even if they are on an active contact.

questions.title: How do you test the failover process and validate readiness before a Region switch?
questions.description: After you have designed your workload to be resilient to the stresses of production, testing is the only way to ensure that it will operate as designed, and deliver the resiliency you expect. Test disaster recovery implementation to validate the implementation and regularly test failover to your workload's DR Region to ensure that RTO and RPO are met. The Global Resiliency page in the Amazon Connect Customer admin website gives a single view of resiliency readiness across linked AWS Regions. The Overall status widget shows Good or Needs attention, the Resource synchronization widget shows which resources are in sync, pending, or need action, and the Traffic Distribution Groups widget shows agent and telephony distribution per TDG with the last Region switch time. Use it to confirm your instance is ready for a Region switch and to resolve synchronization or configuration issues ahead of time.

helpfulResource.displayText: Enable consistent and prompt responses to failure scenarios that are not well understood, by documenting the investigation process in playbooks. Playbooks are the predefined steps performed to identify the factors contributing to a failure scenario. The results from any process step are used to determine the next steps to take until the issue is identified or escalated.

improvementPlan.displayText: Use playbooks to investigate failures

helpfulResource.displayText: Review customer-impacting events, and identify the contributing factors and preventative action items. Use this information to develop mitigations to limit or prevent recurrence. Develop procedures for prompt and effective responses. Communicate contributing factors and corrective actions as appropriate, tailored to target audiences. Have a method to communicate these causes to others as needed.

improvementPlan.displayText: Perform post-incident analysis

helpfulResource.displayText: These include unit tests and integration tests that validate required functionality.

improvementPlan.displayText: Test functional requirements

helpfulResource.displayText: Run tests that inject failures regularly into pre-production and production environments. Hypothesize how your workload will react to the failure, then compare your hypothesis to the testing results and iterate if they do not match. Ensure that production testing does not impact users.

improvementPlan.displayText: Test resiliency using chaos engineering

helpfulResource.displayText: Use game days to regularly exercise your procedures for responding to events and failures as close to production as possible (including in production environments) with the people who will be involved in actual failure scenarios. Game days enforce measures to ensure that production events do not impact users.

improvementPlan.displayText: Considering increasing the frequency at which you're testing the failover process.

choices.title: Conduct failover testing at least every 30 days to validate operational readiness and identify missing upstream dependencies.

helpfulResource.displayText: Regular 30-day failover testing is critical to ensure your ACGR deployment is operationally ready. Testing validates that all upstream dependencies (Lambda functions, third-party integrations, SSO configurations) are properly configured in the alternate region. Customers who skip regular testing often discover missing configurations only during actual incidents - for example, Lambda functions or other upstream dependencies not deployed in the alternate region will prevent successful failover.

improvementPlan.displayText: Establish a 30-day cadence for failover testing. Execute a controlled traffic shift (at minimum 30 percent for 30 minutes) to validate all components function correctly in the alternate region. Document test results and remediate any gaps found. Engage your TAM to confirm testing completion.

choices.title: Enabled the Global Resiliency - View permission in the security profiles of administrators who own resiliency readiness.

helpfulResource.displayText: The Global Resiliency page is visible only to users whose security profile includes the Global Resiliency - View permission. The permission applies only to instances with Global Resiliency enabled.

improvementPlan.displayText: In the admin website, open Security profiles, edit the relevant profile (for example, Admin), select Global Resiliency - View, and save. Confirm the Global Resiliency option appears in the navigation.

choices.title: Review the Overall status widget regularly and confirm it shows Good before any planned Region switch or failover test.

helpfulResource.displayText: The Overall status widget summarizes readiness as one indicator: Good when there are no synchronization or configuration errors, Needs attention when errors are detected. Checking status and Undetermined indicate the status is still loading or could not be retrieved.

improvementPlan.displayText: Add an Overall status check to your failover runbook and pre-switch checklist. When it shows Needs attention, use the Resource synchronization widget to find and fix the affected resources before switching.

choices.title: Resolve every finding in the Resource synchronization widget, using View details for the corrective action.

helpfulResource.displayText: The Resource synchronization widget lists the resources ACGR replicates, the pending sync count per Region (source/replica), and errors such as duplicate resource names, validation constraint mismatches, unassigned phone numbers or users, and resource types supported but not enabled for replication.

improvementPlan.displayText: Choose View details for each resource type with an error and follow the listed action. Allow up to 15 minutes for the widget to reflect a fix. Contact AWS Support if a supported resource type is not enabled for replication.

choices.title: All phone numbers and users are associated with a traffic distribution group (TDG).

helpfulResource.displayText: ACGR requires phone numbers and users to be associated with a TDG so that flows connect to phone numbers in the replica and agents can move across Regions during a Region switch. The readiness page flags unassigned phone numbers and users.

improvementPlan.displayText: In the Resource synchronization widget, choose View details, open the Not assigned to Traffic Distribution Group tab, select the listed phone numbers and users, and associate them with the appropriate TDG.

choices.title: Monitor the Traffic Distribution Groups widget for current agent and telephony distribution and the last Region switch time.

helpfulResource.displayText: The Traffic Distribution Groups widget shows every TDG in the instance with its agent and telephony distribution and the last Region switch time, so you can confirm the expected distribution and track your Region switch test cadence. TDG configuration is changed through the UpdateTrafficDistribution API, not in the widget.

improvementPlan.displayText: Compare the displayed distribution with your intended operating model after every Region switch, and use the last Region switch time to verify failover tests run at least every 30 days.

choices.title: Automated readiness monitoring with the ListReplicationFindings API, with alerts routed to your operations team.

helpfulResource.displayText: Resource synchronization status is also available through the ListReplicationFindings API, so readiness checks can run on a schedule and feed your monitoring and alerting tools.

improvementPlan.displayText: Schedule a job that calls ListReplicationFindings, raises an alert when findings are returned, and records results for operational reviews.

helpfulResource.displayText: Conduct game days regularly

questions.title: ACGR will mirror Amazon Connect resources, what other resources are you mirroring between your two regions?
questions.description: Depending on your DR strategy, you may require some or all of these resources.

helpfulResource.displayText: Global Resiliency lets you replicate a bot in a secondary region. The secondary region can be made active with the automatic replication of the user's bot in both regions. You will have a backup region in case of a regional impairment. Once Global Resiliency is active, new bots created are replicated in the replica AWS region. Amazon Lex is used for multiple purposes in a contact center, including routing, data collection, and self-service. By using Amazon Lex Global Resiliency, you can ensure a consistent customer and agent experience regardless of the active Amazon Connect instance.

improvementPlan.displayText: Ensure that your Amazon Lex v2 bots are configured with Global Resiliency, associated as needed in your replica region, and update your flows to replace any hardcoded Regions with the AwsRegion system attribute. At flow runtime, this attribute is replaced with the Region where the flow is run.

helpfulResource.displayText: Lambda can be used to power self-service, personalization, and automation activities with Amazon Connect. Businesses often want to provide their customers with an exceptional experience, regardless of the region they are operating out of. Deploying Lambda functions across regions allows businesses to provide consistent quality experiences.

improvementPlan.displayText: Ensure that necessary AWS Lambda functions are configured with the same name in both regions, associated as needed in your replica region, and update your flows to replace any hardcoded Regions with the AwsRegion system attribute. At flow runtime, this attribute is replaced with the Region where the flow is run.

helpfulResource.displayText: Choose this option if your resource replication strategy does not follow these best practices.

questions.title: How are you ensuring configuration parity between your two Amazon Connect instances?
questions.description: To accommodate your chosen Global Resiliency strategy, a deployment methodology needs to be defined for your in-scope services.

helpfulResource.displayText: ACGR Global Configuration Management mirrors resources across AWS Regions, including Flows, Flow modules, Users, Routing Profiles, for a complete list access the the More Information link below.

improvementPlan.displayText: ACGR instances onboarded from Nov-2023 have Global Configufation Management enabled by default, previous customers will need to follow a procedure to enable it.

helpfulResource.displayText: If ACGR Global Configuration Management is not enabled (pre Nov-2023), Amazon Connect and other AWS services provide manual back and restore functionality for migrating configurations across environments.

improvementPlan.displayText: Manually replicating config changes is takes time and is error prone. We do not recommend relying on manual configuration of the replica region.

helpfulResource.displayText: Amazon Connect and other AWS services provide APIs for configuring resources programmatically.

improvementPlan.displayText: Although less prone to error, manually invoking APIs is still time consuming and requires appropriate processes to reduce errors.

helpfulResource.displayText: Continuous integration is a DevOps software development practice where developers regularly merge their code changes into a central repository, after which automated builds and tests are run. Continuous delivery is a software development practice where code changes are automatically prepared for a release to production. Continuous delivery expands upon continuous integration by deploying all code changes to a testing environment and/or a production environment after the build stage.

improvementPlan.displayText: Utilizing a CI/CD pipeline helps to reduce the overhead and risk of manually updating and deploying resources. This is the recommended approach for multi-region deployments.

helpfulResource.displayText: Choose this option if your instance synchronization process does not follow these best practices.

questions.title: How are you accounting for your metrics and data between your two instances?
questions.description: Amazon Connect does not currently associate data generated across multiple regions. Ensure you have a design to consolidate your data in order to avoid a disjointed reporting experience. Note: With Global Routing, Amazon Connect provides Global Analytics which offers a natively consolidated view of metrics and Contact Search across both ACGR regions for supported resources.

choices.title: Each instance is treated separately and the data is manually correlated.

improvementPlan.displayText: Consider streaming data into a consolidated data store in order to provide unified metrics.

choices.title: Utilizing a data lake strategy where both instances are writing data to a synchronized location

helpfulResource.displayText: A data lake is a centralized, curated, and secured repository that stores and governs all your structured and unstructured data in its native or transformed formats for analysis. AWS delivers the breadth and depth of services to build a secure, scalable, comprehensive, and cost-effective data lake solution. You can use the AWS services to ingest, store, find, process, and analyze data from a wide variety of sources.

improvementPlan.displayText: For a Zero-ETL option you can implement Amazon Connect analytics data lake.

choices.title: Copying data from replica instance into a S3 bucket in the source region as needed

improvementPlan.displayText: Consider streaming data into a consolidated data store in order to provide unified metrics.

choices.title: Using Global Analytics (consolidated metrics and search) for unified cross-region reporting.

helpfulResource.displayText: With Global Routing, Amazon Connect provides consolidated metrics and Contact Search across both ACGR regions. Real-time metrics UI, historical metrics UI, scheduled reports, GetMetricDataV2 and GetCurrentUserData return a consolidated view, the native Connect dashboards are consolidated for Queues and Agent Performance, GetCurrentMetricData is consolidated only for natively-replicated resources. A new activeRegion filter is available in Contact Search. Remains regional: Agent login/logout reports, Agent Activity Audit, Amazon Connect Data Lake, and Outbound Campaigns dashboard. Consolidated metrics are fetched (not re-replicated) and remain global even after calling UpdateCrossRegionRouting, they revert to single-region only when the instance is offboarded from ACGR.

improvementPlan.displayText: If you have adopted Global Routing, leverage Global Analytics for native consolidated reporting instead of building custom data consolidation. Note the limitations: Data Lake remains regional, and resources not natively replicated (e.g., Outbound Campaigns, Evaluation Forms) will not appear in cross-region reports.

helpfulResource.displayText: Choose this option if your workload does not follow these best practices.

questions.title: How are you ensuring your other AWS services are configured to meet your multi-region strategy?
questions.description: Amazon Connect can leverage a variety of AWS and third-party services to provide an exceptional customer, agent, and admin experience. It is recommended to deploy AWS resources in the same region as your Amazon Connect instances. In the event of an underlying service issue, the recommendation is to redistribute traffic away from the affected service rather than operate in a cross-regional fashion for the best experience.

helpfulResource.displayText: Your AWS account has default quotas, formerly referred to as limits, for each AWS service. Unless otherwise noted, each quota is Region-specific. You can request increases for some quotas, and other quotas cannot be increased.

improvementPlan.displayText: We recommend requesting comparable service quotas for services you expect to utilize in multiple regions.

choices.title: Utilize AWS CloudFormation or similar IaC process

helpfulResource.displayText: AWS CloudFormation lets you model, provision, and manage AWS and third-party resources by treating infrastructure as code.

improvementPlan.displayText: AWS CloudFormation is a service that helps you model and set up Amazon Connect and your other AWS resources so that you can spend less time managing those resources and more time focusing on your applications that run in AWS.

helpfulResource.displayText: Continuous integration is a DevOps software development practice where developers regularly merge their code changes into a central repository, after which automated builds and tests are run. Continuous delivery is a software development practice where code changes are automatically prepared for a release to production. Continuous delivery expands upon continuous integration by deploying all code changes to a testing environment and/or a production environment after the build stage.

improvementPlan.displayText: Utilizing a CI/CD pipeline helps to reduce the overhead and risk of manually updating and deploying resources. This is the recommended approach for multi-region deployments.

questions.title: What resiliency considerations for AWS Lambda have you implemented?
questions.description: Amazon Connect can interact with your own systems and take different paths in contact flows dynamically. To achieve this, invoke Lambda functions in a contact flow, fetch the results, and call your own services or interact with other AWS data stores or services. You can use Lambda functions to either look up or post data to sources outside of Amazon Connect.

choices.title: Managing critical functions through a CI/CD pipeline such as AWS CodePipeline

helpfulResource.displayText: AWS CodePipeline is a continuous integration and continuous delivery service for fast and reliable application and infrastructure updates. CodePipeline builds, tests, and deploys your code every time there is a code change, based on the release process models you define. This enables you to rapidly and reliably deliver features and updates.

improvementPlan.displayText: When deploying functions to the production environment, also ensure you are deploying the function to a replica disaster recovery region. For critical Lambda functions, consider managing these through a CI/CD Pipeline.

choices.title: Utilizing reserved concurrency for your Lambda functions deployed in your replica region.

helpfulResource.displayText: Concurrency is the number of requests that your function is serving at any given time. When your function is invoked, Lambda allocates an instance of it to process the event. When the function code finishes running, it can handle another request. If the function is invoked again while a request is still being processed, another instance is allocated, which increases the function's concurrency. The total concurrency for all of the functions in your account is subject to a per-region quota.

improvementPlan.displayText: Reserved concurrency guarantees the maximum number of concurrent instances for the function. When a function has reserved concurrency, no other function can use that concurrency.

choices.title: Ensure parameters are synchronized with Serverless Application Model (SAM).

helpfulResource.displayText: The AWS Serverless Application Model (SAM) is an open-source framework for building serverless applications. It provides shorthand syntax to express functions, APIs, databases, and event source mappings.

improvementPlan.displayText: Ensure that parameters such as permissions, memory, timeout, environment variables, and other options are synchronized.

questions.title: What resiliency considerations for Amazon Lex have you implemented?
questions.description: Utilizing Amazon Lex with Amazon Connect allows you to build conversational interactions that feel natural to your customers. You can capture spoken input as well as numeric input, allowing customers to choose how they interact with your contact flow. Amazon Lex also powers chat conversations, allowing conversational interaction with a virtual agent and rich interactive messaging.

helpfulResource.displayText: Global Resiliency lets you replicate a bot in a secondary region. The secondary region can be made active with the automatic replication of the user's bot in both regions. You will have a backup region in case of a regional impairment. Once Global Resiliency is active, new bots created are replicated in the replica AWS region. Amazon Lex is used for multiple purposes in a contact center, including routing, data collection, and self-service. By using Amazon Lex Global Resiliency, you can ensure a consistent customer and agent experience regardless of the active Amazon Connect instance.

improvementPlan.displayText: Ensure that your Amazon Lex v2 bots are configured with Global Resiliency, associated as needed in your replica region, and update your flows to replace any hardcoded Regions with the AwsRegion system attribute. At flow runtime, this attribute is replaced with the Region where the flow is run.

helpfulResource.displayText: Choose this option if your workload does not follow these best practices.

questions.title: What resiliency considerations for Amazon S3 have you implemented?
questions.description: Amazon Connect uses Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) to store recorded conversations, chat transcripts, exported reports, and contact flows. When you set up Amazon Connect, it creates default buckets for these requirements, or you can point it to existing Amazon S3 infrastructure. You can also manage the Amazon S3 policies to move data to Amazon S3 Glacier for less expensive long-term storage.

helpfulResource.displayText: Amazon S3 cross-region replication enables automatic asynchronous copy of objects between Amazon S3 buckets. Buckets configured for object replication may be owned by the same AWS account or different accounts. You can copy objects between different AWS regions or within the same region.

improvementPlan.displayText: If you want unified access to your Amazon Connect data stored in S3, consider using Amazon S3 cross-region replication.

choices.title: Amazon S3 Replication Time Control (S3 RTC)

helpfulResource.displayText: You can use Amazon S3 Replication Time Control (S3 RTC) to replicate your data in the same AWS Region or in different regions over a predictable period. Amazon S3 RTC replicates 99.99 percent of new objects stored in Amazon S3 in 15 minutes.

improvementPlan.displayText: Within your contact flow, you can prompt for additional information and, if they need to reach an agent, you can use the contact flow configuration to place them in the appropriate queue.

helpfulResource.displayText: To sync buckets and replicate existing objects, use Batch Replication as an on-demand replication action. Batch Replication replicates existing objects to different buckets as an on-demand option.

improvementPlan.displayText: When you need to move your data as needed, consider using Batch Replication versus live replication.

helpfulResource.displayText: Amazon S3 Multi-Region Access Points provide a single global endpoint to access a data set that spans multiple S3 buckets in different AWS Regions. This allows you to build multi-region applications with the same simple architecture used in a single region, and then to run those applications anywhere in the world..

improvementPlan.displayText: Consider using Amazon S3 Multi-Region Access Points when your application requires requests to be made to an S3 Multi-Region Access Point's global endpoint automatically route over the AWS global network to the S3 bucket with the lowest network latency.

questions.title: How do you dynamically adapt to out-of-office conditions?
questions.description: Other AWS services can be used to augment, monitor, or operationalize your Amazon Connect deployment. Ensure you are considering these resources when architecting Amazon Connect Global Resiliency.

helpfulResource.displayText: DynamoDB global tables are a collection of one or more replica tables, all owned by a single AWS account. A replica table is a single DynamoDB table that functions as a part of a global table. Each replica stores the same set of data items. Any given global table can only have one replica table per AWS region.

improvementPlan.displayText: If an AWS region becomes isolated or degraded, your application and Amazon Connect can re-distribute traffic to a replica healthy region. By replicating data across regions, the active Amazon Connect instance can access data in region to perform necessary interaction handling functions. This architecture carries additional costs, but offers strong redundancy with eventually-consistent data replication in an active-active topology..

helpfulResource.displayText: You can create cross-account cross-region dashboards, which summarize your CloudWatch data from multiple AWS accounts and multiple Regions into one dashboard.

improvementPlan.displayText: Cross-account cross-region dashboards enables centralized visibility of your CloudWatch metrics, logs and the health/ performance of applications running in several Regions. CloudWatch metric math allows you to query multiple metrics for aggregation from multiple accounts and Regions. This ensures monitoring visibility in the event of a failover scenario. CloudWatch also provides metrics for concurrent call, chat and task quotas..

questions.title: Have you evaluated and prepared for Amazon Connect Global Routing adoption?
questions.description: Amazon Connect Global Routing enables contacts originated in one AWS Region to be answered by agents active in a second AWS Region, enabling true active-active operation across ACGR-linked instances. The routing engine evaluates agents from both regions simultaneously and directs contacts to the optimal agent regardless of which region agents are distributed to, extending advanced features like Threshold Based Routing, Claim Agent, and User Matching Rules across both regions. Distributing traffic and agents 50/50 reduces blast radius and continuously exercises dependencies in both regions. Note: today activeRegion and originRegion are always identical because contacts are not moved between regions yet, they will diverge when queued-callback failover launches. Adopting Global Routing requires updates to your CCP, third-party integrations, event stream pipelines, and awareness of feature limitations. For more information, refer to the Amazon Connect Admin Guide: Global Routing Across ACGR Regions.

choices.title: Updated custom CCP with Streams JS (secondaryCCPUrl and enableGlobalResiliency configured).

helpfulResource.displayText: With Global Routing, the source and replica instance share the same alias differentiated by their regional subdomain (e.g., us-east-1.example.my.connect.aws and us-west-2.example.my.connect.aws). Your custom CCP must be updated with the secondaryCCPUrl and enableGlobalResiliency flag to handle cross-region contacts. Maintain a failover logic to the old replica instance domain during the transition phase.

improvementPlan.displayText: Update your Streams JS CCP initialization to include secondaryCCPUrl and enableGlobalResiliency: true. Update firewall rules to allow-list the new regional subdomain. Maintain backward-compatible failover logic during transition.

choices.title: Updated third-party integrations and Workspace apps for new regional alias and cross-region handling.

helpfulResource.displayText: Third-party integrations consuming the Connect instance URL must be updated to use the new alias. Workspace apps calling mutation operations (UpdateContactAttributes, TransferContact) must verify the 'region' flag in the Connect SDK and make API calls to the contact's originating region. Apps using read-only APIs (SearchUsers, GetCurrentMetricData, DescribeContact) will work without updates.

improvementPlan.displayText: Audit all third-party integrations for instance URL dependencies. Update mutation API calls to check the contact's region flag. Add application URLs as approved domains in both regions to avoid CSP errors for cross-region app invocation.

choices.title: Configured event stream pipelines to consume CTRs, AES, and CES from both regions.

helpfulResource.displayText: With Global Routing: Contact Event Streams (CES) are emitted in both regions regardless of contact origin. Agent Event Streams (AES) are region-specific, only available in the region the agent is active in. Contact Trace Records (CTRs) remain in the contact's originating region. A new GlobalResiliencyMetadata object appears in CES, AES, and CTR carrying activeRegion, originRegion, and trafficDistributionGroupId (the JSON payload uses camelCase). AES additionally carries AgentCrossRegionRoutingConfiguration (ConfiguredRegions and CurrentRegion). Build consolidation logic to combine CTRs and AES from both regions for unified reporting and WFM integration.

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement integration pipelines in both regions to consume AES and CTRs. Use GlobalResiliencyMetadata to identify the contact's Region (the contact stays in its origin Region for its whole lifecycle), and the agent's ActiveRegion (AgentInfo in CES, Agent in CTR, AgentCrossRegionRoutingConfiguration in AES) to identify where the contact is handled. Remember: mutation operations on a contact (UpdateContactAttributes, TransferContact) must target the contact's origin Region, mutation operations on an agent (PutUserStatus) must target the agent's active Region, read operations (DescribeContact) can target either Region. CES provides a consolidated view, but build pipelines in both regions for resiliency.

choices.title: Updated Kinesis Video Streams (KVS) integration to consume audio from the contact's originating region.

helpfulResource.displayText: With Global Routing, Amazon Connect streams KVS audio in the contact's originating region. For example, if a contact originates in us-east-1 and is routed to an agent in us-west-2, the KVS audio will be available in us-east-1. If you use KVS for voicemail capture or third-party call analytics, you need integration pipelines in both regions.

improvementPlan.displayText: Develop KVS integration pipelines in both regions since contacts can originate in either region. Ensure voicemail, call recording, and third-party analytics systems can consume KVS streams from the contact's originating region, not the agent's region.

choices.title: Aware of features not supported with Global Routing and have workarounds in place.

helpfulResource.displayText: Not all Amazon Connect features are supported for active-active operation with Global Routing. Key limitations: advanced chat capabilities (quick responses, chat rehydration) are not available for cross-region contacts, Outbound Campaigns and Cases are not supported with Global Routing, async channels (tasks, emails, cases) are regional. For chat, it is recommended to run blended agents in a single region and use separate TDGs for voice-only agents distributed across regions.

improvementPlan.displayText: Review the full list of features not supported with Global Routing. Design your TDG strategy to keep chat/blended agents in a single region while distributing voice-only agents across regions. Plan workarounds for unsupported features or keep those workloads regional until full support is available.

choices.title: Designed Traffic Distribution Group (TDG) strategy to support active-active agent distribution for Global Routing.

helpfulResource.displayText: With Global Routing, agents can be distributed across regions (e.g., 50-50) via TDGs, and the routing engine evaluates agents from both regions simultaneously. Design separate TDGs for different use cases: voice-only agents distributed across regions, blended (voice+chat) agents in a single region, and separate TDGs for test numbers. The routing engine supports cross-region Threshold Based Routing, Claim Agent, and User Matching Rules.

improvementPlan.displayText: Design your TDG strategy to segment agents by channel capability. Create separate TDGs for blended agents (single-region) and voice-only agents (multi-region). Validate that your Threshold Based Routing, Claim Agent, and User Matching Rules work correctly in a cross-region scenario. Test with incremental traffic distribution before going to full active-active.

choices.title: Validated Global Analytics reporting provides a consolidated cross-region view for supported metrics and dashboards.

helpfulResource.displayText: With Global Routing, GetMetricDataV2 and GetCurrentUserData return a consolidated view regardless of which Region you invoke them from, and GetCurrentMetricData is consolidated only for natively-replicated resources. Real-time metrics, historical metrics and scheduled reports provide a consolidated view. Contact Search allows supervisors to search and view contacts handled across paired ACGR instances. Some features remain regional: Agent login/logout reports, Agent Activity Audit, Amazon Connect Data Lake, and the Outbound Campaigns dashboard.

improvementPlan.displayText: Validate that your reporting dashboards and APIs return the expected consolidated view. Note that Agent login/logout reports, Agent Activity Audit, Data Lake and the Outbound Campaigns dashboard remain regional, and GetCurrentMetricData is consolidated only for natively-replicated resources. Ensure any custom reporting solutions that consume metrics APIs are updated to handle the consolidated cross-region data. Test Contact Search to verify cross-region contact visibility.

choices.title: Aware of the UpdateCrossRegionRouting API to stop or restart cross-region routing on demand.

helpfulResource.displayText: UpdateCrossRegionRouting is a new API that stops or restarts cross-region routing on demand. It is a last resort to contain issues within a region (poison-pill situations) during degraded conditions. It only prevents cross-region routing, consolidated reporting continues to operate globally. Failover of agents and telephony traffic is still performed separately with UpdateTrafficDistribution. Available only for instances onboarded to Global Routing.

improvementPlan.displayText: Document in your runbook when and how to invoke UpdateCrossRegionRouting (IsolatedRegions is true to isolate, false to integrate). For agent populations relying on features not yet supported for cross-region handling (e.g. Salesforce integration), disable cross-region routing before shifting those agents and their traffic during failover.

choices.title: Established CloudWatch monitoring and alarms across both ACGR regions.

helpfulResource.displayText: Monitor both ACGR regions with Amazon CloudWatch. Track Amazon Connect service metrics, concurrent calls, queue and agent metrics, and the health of dependent services (Lambda, Lex, third-party integrations) in each region. Set alarms so you can detect regional degradation early and decide when to shift traffic or isolate cross-region routing. The ACGR workshop walks through recommended Connect monitoring.

improvementPlan.displayText: Build CloudWatch dashboards and alarms in BOTH regions covering Connect metrics and all dependent services. Validate alarms during your 30-day failover tests. Follow the ACGR workshop monitoring module to establish a baseline observability setup for cross-region operations.

choices.title: Confirmed WFM readiness for active-active (AES and Data Lake are regional, and FCS does not support ACGR yet).

helpfulResource.displayText: In active-active operation, some data sources are not consolidated across regions. Agent Event Streams (AES) remain region-specific (each region emits only its own agent activity) and Amazon Connect Data Lake remains regional. Your Workforce Management (WFM) system must therefore consume and combine data from both regions to get a complete view of agent activity and contact volume. In addition, Amazon Connect Forecast, Capacity Planning and Scheduling (FCS) does not support ACGR yet, so it cannot produce a unified cross-region forecast or schedule today.

improvementPlan.displayText: Confirm your WFM integration ingests AES and contact records from BOTH regions and consolidates them before running active-active. Do not rely on Data Lake or AES for a single consolidated view, they are regional. Until Forecast, Capacity Planning and Scheduling supports ACGR, plan forecasting and scheduling per region or through your external WFM, and account for cross-region routing when interpreting the numbers.

helpfulResource.displayText: Choose this option if you have not evaluated or prepared for Global Routing adoption.
